what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat Pseudobulbar Affect (PBA). PBA causes sudden, uncontrollable episodes of laughing or crying that do not match how you actually feel. It happens in people with certain brain or nervous system conditions, such as multiple sclerosis (MS) or ALS (Lou Gehrig's disease). This medicine helps reduce how often and how severely these episodes happen.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with or without food. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsule. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember. The capsule contains two medicines working together — do not take them separately.
dosing: You will start by taking ONE capsule once a day for the first 7 days. After that, if your doctor says it is okay, you will take ONE capsule TWICE a day (every 12 hours). Always follow your doctor's exact instructions. Do not take more than 2 capsules in one day.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — BUT only if it has been less than 4 hours since your scheduled time. If it has been longer than 4 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep away from moisture and heat. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date printed on the package.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT take this medicine with certain other medicines without talking to your doctor first, including: other medicines that contain quinidine, medicines that affect heart rhythm (such as amiodarone or sotalol), some antidepressants called MAOIs (such as phenelzine or tranylcypromine — wait at least 14 days after stopping an MAOI before starting this medicine), certain antifungal medicines (such as ketoconazole or itraconazole), and some HIV medicines. Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice, as they can increase the amount of medicine in your body. Limit or avoid alcohol while taking this medicine, as it may increase side effects like dizziness. Tell all of your doctors and your pharmacist about every medicine, vitamin, and supplement you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or get emergency help if you have: a fast, slow, or irregular heartbeat or pounding in your chest; fainting or feeling like you might faint; severe dizziness; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as hives, rash, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or trouble breathing; fever, muscle stiffness, confusion, or sweating (these could be signs of a rare but serious condition called serotonin syndrome); signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain; or unusual thoughts or feelings of self-harm. Also call your doctor if your PBA episodes are not improving or are getting worse.
when_it_works: Most people notice fewer and less intense episodes of uncontrollable laughing or crying within the first 1 to 2 weeks of taking the full twice-daily dose. Some people may take a little longer to see the full benefit. Keep taking the medicine as prescribed even if you do not see immediate improvement. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as the safety of this medicine during pregnancy and breastfeeding is not fully known. OLDER ADULTS (65+): Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness and falls — use extra caution. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Your doctor may need to monitor you more closely or adjust your dose if you have kidney or liver disease. HEART CONDITIONS: Tell your doctor if you have a history of heart problems, irregular heart rhythm (arrhythmia), or low potassium or magnesium levels, as this medicine can affect your heart rhythm.
